source.title: Deep Information Propagation
source.authors: Samuel S. Schoenholz; Justin Gilmer; Surya Ganguli; Jascha Sohl-Dickstein

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains randomly initialized networks and measures training accuracy across depth and initialization settings, directly testing trainability.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy outcomes are reported for the paper's own experiments. Values in the figures are not numerically recoverable from the text; the paper's text describes the aggregate outcomes and depth relationship. The paper also discusses prior initialization schemes, but those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V4 by varying initialization variance and network depth and measuring training accuracy and speed. It is an original source for V4, so no verdict labels are assigned. Its fully connected networks do not test V1's convolutional-network claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors report trainability approximately when L ≲ 6ξc, faster training nearer criticality, and a finite maximum trainable depth with dropout. They distinguish preservation of input and gradient correlations from preservation of gradient magnitude alone.
record.recipe_differences: Trains randomly initialized fully connected networks and measures training accuracy as depth, weight variance, optimizer, dataset, duration and dropout vary; the paper presents this as an empirical test of its mean-field trainability predictions.
record.method_sensitivity: Trainability changes with depth and weight variance; the authors report a relationship with the correlation depth scale, faster training closer to criticality, and a dropout-dependent upper bound on trainable depth. The paper reports no obvious dependence on dataset, duration or minimizer for the plotted no-dropout relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: Successfully trained fully connected networks attain 100% training accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR-10; this does not establish near-zero error for the convolutional networks specified in V1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some randomly initialized fully connected networks can fit MNIST and CIFAR-10 completely under suitable depth and initialization settings.

record.problems: Training-accuracy maps are presented as figures without numerical values for individual settings. Experiments use fully connected networks; the paper states its analysis applies directly only to fully connected feed-forward networks.

untested.parts: The specified convolutional networks, CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and model-size or regularization comparisons are not tested. Fully connected CIFAR-10 and MNIST results do not establish this version.
Two-layer ReLU teacher–student problems, spurious minima frequencies, and extra student neurons are not tested.
Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks, special deep plain-network initializations, and Fixup are not tested.

No orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison, orthogonal convolution kernels, or 10000-layer training. Experiments cover fully connected networks up to 300 layers; the framework is explicitly not established for unbounded activations such as ReLU.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability training are not tested.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup training experiment.

missing.what: Gradient measurements in 240-layer, width-300 random networks: gradients vanish in the ordered phase and explode in the chaotic phase as initialization variance changes; measured gradient depth scales agree with theory, with finite-size deviations near criticality.
Additional training-accuracy maps at 45, 304, 2048, and 13780 steps for SGD and RMSProp provide initialization-dependent training-speed comparisons absent from the extracted rows.

record.verdict_notes: V4 is explicitly attributed to this study, so its results receive no supports, limits_scope, or challenges labels. Individual accuracy values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. The broad statement about 100% training accuracy must be read alongside the explicitly reported low-accuracy and untrainable regions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fully connected networks on MNIST and CIFAR10, not CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, or smaller-model and regularization comparisons.
Does not compare orthogonal with Gaussian initializations or test orthogonal convolution kernels at 10,000 layers. Tests weight-variance settings in fully connected random networks.

relation.reason: Its training experiments directly test the relationship between initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.

tranche.reason: This original V4 source measures training accuracy while varying initialization variance and depth in randomly initialized fully connected networks.

source_check.notes: The authors report approximate trainability at L ≲ 6ξc and faster training nearer criticality. The 100% accuracy statement and approximate dropout depth limit are aggregate descriptions, not numerical results for every plotted setting.
